title: Shot on Goal
story: A player passes to the coach on the wing, sprints forward for the return, and finishes first-time without a touch to set it up.
setup: Coach stands wide of the goal, a few yards outside the width of the area. Players line up with balls at the top of the area, one at a time.
instructions: The player passes to the coach on the wing, then sprints toward goal.
The coach plays the ball back into the player's path.
The player strikes the first-time shot on goal without controlling it first.
Rotate quickly to the back of the line; run two lines at once when numbers allow to keep the wait brief.
coach_lens: Notice the run timed to arrive as the ball does, a firm first pass to the coach and a committed strike rather than a tentative poke.
questions: Where did you want the return pass to meet you?

simplify: Allow one controlling touch before the shot.
Move the coach closer for an easier return pass.
challenge: Serve the return pass slightly behind the run so the player must adjust.
Add a second coach or line on the opposite wing.
low_attendance: Run one line and let players go twice each.
high_attendance: Run two lines from both wings into the same goal to halve the wait.
limited_equipment: Use a cone-gate target if a full goal is not available.

safety: Only one player shoots at a time; keep the line back from the shooting lane.
Check the goal is secured or weighted before shooting drills begin.

source.title: How to help 5-11s develop their skills on the ball
source.reviewer_notes: Coach-authored wing-combination finishing pattern developed and field-tested with a real youth team, applying England Football guidance on realistic, repeatable ball-skill practice. No source wording or artwork reproduced.
